title: Evolution of Plate Tectonics Theory
subject: Geography
description: This diagram illustrates the historical development of the Plate Tectonics theory, from Continental Drift to Seafloor Spreading, culminating in the modern understanding, including key proponents, evidence, and shortcomings.
mermaidCode:
graph TD
A[Continental Drift (Wegener, 1912)] --> B{Evidence}
B --> B1(Jigsaw fit of coastlines)
B --> B2(Matching geological formations)
B --> B3(Identical fossils)
B --> B4(Glacial tillites)
A --> A1[Shortcoming: Lacked convincing mechanism]
A --> C[Convectional Current Theory (Holmes, 1930s)]
C --> C1(Mantle convection currents as driving force)
C --> D[Seafloor Spreading (Hess, 1960s)]
D --> D1(New oceanic crust at mid-oceanic ridges)
D --> D2(Crust consumed at subduction zones)
D --> E{Evidence}
E --> E1(Magnetic stripes)
E --> E2(Age progression of ocean floor)
E --> E3(Heat flow anomalies)
E --> E4(Sediment thickness patterns)
D --> F[Modern Theory of Plate Tectonics]
F --> F1(Lithosphere broken into plates)
F --> F2(Plates float on asthenosphere)
